title: Hyperpolarized Noble Gases
summary: Hyperpolarization breaks the signal free of the Boltzmann factor: SEOP or MEOP drives noble gas nuclear polarization to 0.2 to 0.9 against the 2.7 x 10^-6 that 129Xe would hold at 3 T and 37 C, a gain near 10^5 that more than pays for a gas being about 1000-fold thinner in spins than tissue water. 3He has the larger gyromagnetic ratio, 32.43 MHz/T against 11.777 MHz/T, and five times the ADC, but its only source is tritium decay; the post-2008 price rise pushed clinical lung MRI onto 129Xe, which is now the approved agent. 129Xe earns that position by dissolving: at 3 T the lung spectrum carries gas at 0 ppm, membrane at 197.6 ppm and red blood cells at 218.2 ppm, and the RBC to membrane ratio is a direct readout of alveolar-capillary transfer. The magnetization is spent once, so every RF pulse and every second of breath-hold in 100 mmHg of oxygen is signal you never get back.

facts.label: The four nuclei
facts.value: 3He spin 1/2, 32.43 MHz/T, 48.65 MHz at 1.5T; 129Xe spin 1/2, 11.777 MHz/T, 17.66 MHz at 1.5T and 35.33 MHz at 3T; 131Xe spin 3/2, 3.51 MHz/T; 83Kr spin 9/2, 1.64 MHz/T. Natural abundance 1.37 ppm of helium, 26.4 percent, 21.2 percent and 11.5 percent respectively
facts.note: 131Xe is the only stable noble gas nucleus with a positive gyromagnetic ratio, so 3He, 129Xe and 83Kr all precess opposite to 1H; 3He is manufactured rather than mined, and 129Xe and 83Kr are isotopically enriched, 129Xe typically to 83 to 87 percent.

facts.label: Thermal versus hyperpolarized polarization
facts.value: 129Xe thermal polarization is 2.7 x 10^-6 at 3 T and 37 C and about 1.4 x 10^-6 at 1.5 T; SEOP delivers roughly 25 percent for a 1 L clinical accumulation and about 30 percent for 100 mL preclinical volumes, with modern systems routinely at or above 30 percent for 1 L
facts.note: The gain is near 10^5, but it is a fixed stock of magnetization, not a renewable equilibrium, so the design variable becomes signal budget rather than SNR per unit time.

facts.label: Spin exchange optical pumping, alkali choice
facts.value: Rb D1 at 794.8 nm is standard for 129Xe; K D1 at 770.1 nm and Cs D1 at 894.3 nm are the alternatives. In K-Rb hybrid cells for 3He the spin-exchange efficiency approaches 1/4, an order of magnitude above pure Rb, with best results at Rb to K vapour density ratios of 2 to 6
facts.note: 129Xe polarizes through both binary Rb-Xe collisions and longer-lived van der Waals molecules, which is why continuous-flow Xe SEOP runs at roughly 1 to 3 percent xenon in N2 and He at flows near 1 SLM rather than in pure xenon.

facts.label: Metastability exchange optical pumping for 3He
facts.value: 1083 nm pumping of the 2 3S1 metastable in a weak discharge at about 1 mbar, then metastability-exchange collisions to the ground state. About 80 percent polarization at 1.33 mbar and 25 percent at 67 mbar at 1.5 T; above 80 percent at 2, 3 and 4 T, reaching 89 percent at 3 T
facts.note: MEOP polarizes in seconds to minutes but only at low pressure, so the gas must be compressed by roughly three orders of magnitude to reach imaging pressure, and that compressor is where polarization, throughput and money are lost.

facts.label: The 3He supply problem
facts.value: 3He is a decay product of tritium, half-life 12.3 y, separated from weapons-stockpile tritium processing. Market price ran 100 to 200 USD per liter before the 2008 shortage and was quoted above 2000 USD per liter afterwards, with DOE selling around 350 to 400 USD per liter
facts.note: At a 300 mL to 1 L dose per scan, with neutron detection outbidding imaging for the same gas, the economics ended 3He human lung MRI; natural xenon costs a few dollars per liter and enriched 129Xe is still orders of magnitude cheaper per dose.

facts.label: 129Xe dissolved-phase spectrum, three compartments
facts.value: At 3 T: gas 0 ppm, membrane (barrier) 197.6 +/- 0.3 ppm, red blood cells 218.2 +/- 0.5 ppm. Multi-site healthy reference amplitudes membrane/gas 0.97 +/- 0.27 percent and RBC/gas 0.48 +/- 0.20 percent. Global T2* at 3 T is 0.99 +/- 0.04 ms for membrane and 1.04 +/- 0.03 ms for RBC, near 2 ms at 1.5 T
facts.note: Total dissolved signal is about 1.5 percent of the gas signal and its T2* is near 1 ms, so dissolved-phase work is an SNR and TE problem first; older papers put the RBC peak at 211 ppm, which is mostly a referencing difference, so always state what was called 0 ppm.

facts.label: RBC to membrane ratio as a gas-exchange readout
facts.value: Healthy 0.49 +/- 0.11 at 3 T pooled across Siemens, Philips and GE sites; 0.55 +/- 0.13 in the original 1.5 T cohort. In IPF the ratio falls 3.3-fold to 0.16 +/- 0.03, from a 52 percent drop in RBC signal and a 58 percent rise in barrier signal
facts.note: The ratio is dimensionless and cancels polarization, dose, coil loading and receive gain, which is why it transfers between sites and vendors far better than any single compartment amplitude.

facts.label: Cardiogenic RBC oscillation
facts.value: RBC signal amplitude oscillates with the cardiac cycle at 10.0 +/- 2.5 percent peak to peak in healthy adults, resolved by acquiring one dissolved-phase FID every 20 ms
facts.note: The oscillation tracks capillary blood volume across the cardiac cycle and is elevated in IPF and pulmonary vascular disease; sample slower than about 50 ms and it aliases into the mean instead of appearing as a waveform.

facts.label: Gas-phase T1 and oxygen depolarization
facts.value: 129Xe gas-phase T1 is hours in a clean sealed cell, 2.55 +/- 0.22 h measured for bulk gas, but about 20 s in the lung. The 129Xe oxygen relaxivity is 0.482 s^-1 amagat^-1; for 3He the calibration is T1 = 2.61 bar.s divided by pO2, giving about 20 s at an alveolar pO2 of 0.13 bar
facts.note: Oxygen sets the breath-hold budget for both gases and is simultaneously the contrast mechanism for pO2 mapping; a 16 s breath-hold has already spent more than half the polarization before the last phase encode.

facts.label: 129Xe in blood, T1 and solubility
facts.value: T1 in blood is about 4 s deoxygenated and 6 to 13 s oxygenated; reported ranges are 6 to 8 s arterial and 3 to 4 s venous, and this is a genuine range across studies. Ostwald coefficients at 37 C are about 0.09 in saline and plasma, about 0.2 in red blood cells, about 0.1 in parenchymal tissue and 1.7 to 1.9 in olive oil, giving a blood to gas partition coefficient of 0.13 to 0.20
facts.note: Deoxyhemoglobin is paramagnetic, so venous relaxation is faster and increasing oxygenation shifts the RBC resonance to higher frequency; the lipid affinity is why xenon crosses the blood-brain barrier freely and why it is an anesthetic.

facts.label: 129Xe in the brain
facts.value: Human head spectrum at 1.5 T resolves peaks near 187, 192.5, 195.4, 199 and 216.2 ppm, assigned to non-brain soft tissue, white matter, gray matter, CSF and blood. Typical protocol is 500 mL inhaled with a 20 s breath-hold and a dynamic spectrum every 2 s
facts.note: Gray and white matter differ by only about 3 ppm and brain dissolved signal is orders of magnitude below lung gas signal, so brain xenon is spectroscopy or coarse CSI, not lung-grade imaging.

facts.label: Dose and breath-hold
facts.value: Approved target dose is 75 to 100 mL Dose Equivalent inhaled in a single 10 to 15 s breath-hold; 100 mL DE is about 390 mL of 86 percent enriched gas at 30 percent polarization. Research protocols use up to 1 L from a Tedlar bag inhaled from FRC or RV. Xenon MAC is about 71 percent and noticeable sedation starts above roughly 30 percent inhaled fraction
facts.note: Dose Equivalent is volume times polarization times enrichment, so bag volume alone tells you nothing; transient dizziness, tingling and mild euphoria are expected and self-limited, and a brief SpO2 dip is normal.

facts.label: Diffusion and ventilation reference values
facts.value: Global ADC at 1.5 T in healthy nonsmokers is 0.190 +/- 0.017 cm2/s for 3He and 0.038 +/- 0.003 cm2/s for 129Xe. Ventilation defect percent in healthy adults is 1.6 +/- 1.2 percent with an upper limit of normal near 2.0 percent, age-stratified to 1.3 percent at 18 to 39 y, 2.5 percent at 40 to 59 y and 3.8 percent at 60 to 79 y
facts.note: The five-fold ADC gap is the free diffusion coefficient of the gas, not lung physiology; 3He and 129Xe ADC correlate at r = 0.92, so xenon inherits the emphysema sensitivity but needs its own b values and its own normative data.

facts.label: 131Xe and 83Kr, surface-sensitive quadrupolar relaxation
facts.value: 131Xe is spin 3/2 with Q = -11.4 fm2 (-0.114 barn), polarized to 2.2 percent in early work and 7.6 +/- 1.5 percent more recently. 83Kr is spin 9/2 with Q near +0.26 barn; T1 in excised rat lung runs 5.3 +/- 1.9 s in trachea, 3.0 +/- 0.9 s in main stem bronchus, 1.1 +/- 0.2 s in parenchyma next to the major airways and 0.9 +/- 0.1 s in peripheral parenchyma
facts.note: Relaxation runs through the quadrupole coupling to electric field gradients generated at the gas-surface interface, so T1 reports surface to volume ratio; SQUARE T1 lengthens in elastase-induced emphysema as alveolar surface is destroyed, and 131Xe additionally shows a surface- and field-dependent quadrupolar splitting that water vapour reduces.

practice: Shim and set the center frequency on 1H, then switch channels. 129Xe sits at 35.33 MHz at 3 T, outside the body coil, so transmit is through a dedicated vest or birdcage and the flip angle has to be calibrated on the actual dose, never assumed from a 1H reference.

Treat the magnetization as a fixed bank account. n pulses at flip angle a leave cos^n(a) of the longitudinal magnetization, so pick the angle from the number of views, not from habit; a ventilation GRE typically sits near 5 to 10 degrees.

For gas exchange, excite near 208 ppm, midway between the 197.6 ppm membrane and 218.2 ppm RBC peaks. At 3 T that is a 7.35 kHz offset from gas, at 1.5 T 3.67 kHz; a short sinc of roughly 0.7 ms covers both dissolved peaks while suppressing gas.

Measure polarization on a calibration station immediately before delivery and record it with the scan. Keep the bag away from stray gradients and ferromagnetic clutter, and minimise the time from polarizer to inhalation.
Coach the breath-hold to a defined lung volume, FRC or RV per protocol. Gas-exchange ratios depend on inflation, so inconsistent lung volume is a leading source of between-visit variance.
Record hemoglobin concentration. RBC-derived metrics scale with it and a published adjustment exists; without it, anemia reads as impaired gas transfer.
Use a thermally polarized 129Xe phantom for QA. It separates coil and receive-chain performance from polarizer performance, which is the ambiguity that otherwise eats multi-site studies.
Sample the dissolved FID about every 20 ms if you want the cardiogenic RBC oscillation amplitude rather than only its time average.
pitfalls: Oxygen. At an alveolar pO2 near 100 mmHg the gas-phase T1 is about 20 s, so a long breath-hold has spent most of the polarization before the last k-space line; oxygen back-diffusing into a dose bag on the bench does the same thing more slowly.

Gas-phase contamination of dissolved-phase images. The gas peak is roughly 70 times larger than the summed dissolved peaks, so excitation sidelobes and off-resonance leakage put airway signal where you are reading barrier uptake. Inspect the spectrum, not just the image.
Flip-angle error is unrecoverable. There is no steady state and no second dose, so a wrong transmit gain does not merely lower SNR, it can burn the whole bag on the first few views.

Negative gyromagnetic ratio. 3He, 129Xe and 83Kr precess opposite to 1H, so phase accumulation, Dixon phase evolution and flow encoding all change sign against vendor 1H conventions; the classic symptom is a 1-point Dixon that swaps RBC and membrane.

Chemical shift referencing. RBC values of 211, 217 and 218 ppm all appear in print, and most of the spread is what was called 0 ppm, not physiology; blood oxygenation genuinely moves the RBC peak as well, so quote the gas reference and the oxygenation state.

131Xe and 83Kr lose their polarization on the way to the magnet. Quadrupolar surface relaxation gives T1 of seconds or less and the low gyromagnetic ratios, 3.51 and 1.64 MHz/T, cost detection sensitivity on top of that, so transfer time is the binding constraint on the whole experiment.
